name: Bojuka Bog
oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
When this land enters, exile target player's graveyard.
{T}: Add {B}.
blocked_sentences: When this land enters, exile target player's graveyard.

needs.what: let a selector scope a non-battlefield zone to a player chosen as a target, so `exile` with `{"zone": "graveyard", "count": "all", "player": {"target": "t1"}}` (a target spec of kind `player`) empties exactly that one player's graveyard. Concretely: `_zone_owners` in effects/selectors.py should accept a player spec resolved through `select_players` -- which already understands `{"target": ...}` -- instead of only the three literal controller words, and `validate_selector` must let that key through.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `_zone_owners` reads `controller`, and `validate_selector` restricts it to "you", "opponent" or "any" -- none of which is "the one player this trigger targeted", and `"any"` with `count: "all"` exiles every graveyard, which is Relic of Progenitus rather than Bojuka Bog. The `{"target": "t1"}` selector shorthand cannot stand in either: `EffectContext.target_oids` keeps only refs with `kind == "object"`, so a player target seeds an empty pool. `select_players` does resolve `{"target": ...}` to a targeted player, but only ops carrying a `player` spec (`draw`, `mill`, `discard`, `look_at_hand`) call it, and `exile` takes only an `objects` selector.
